posts.text: I am proud to recognize 23 remarkable Idahoans with the 2026 Spirit of Freedom: Idaho Veterans Service Award for their extraordinary dedication to serving our nation and supporting our veterans.  Since creating this award in 2002, I have had the privilege of presenting 447 awards to compassionate veterans and volunteers whose selfless service reflects the very best of the Gem State. https://t.co/KaGy7zPUlf

November is Military Family Month, a time to honor the quiet strength, resilience and unwavering dedication of our nation’s military families.  Behind every brave servicemember stands a family enduring long separations, frequent relocations and the constant strain of sacrifice to support our country's freedom.  We owe these heroic families a debt of gratitude that can never fully be repaid.  Thank you to our military families in Idaho and across America for your steadfast commitment to our country.
https://t.co/bKQBR4F7kR

We owe it to our brave Idaho veterans to ensure federal programs deliver the high-quality care, housing assistance and disability benefits they have earned. From reducing disability claims backlogs to enacting legislation like the Disabled Veterans Housing Support Act, we have made real progress on removing administrative barriers for veteran families. I will continue fighting to pass vital measures like the Major Richard Star Act and the End Veterans Overdose Act to ensure our nation's heroes receive the full support and respect they deserve.

During National Veterans Small Business Week, we celebrate the entrepreneurial spirit of our nation’s veterans. Idaho’s veteran-owned businesses account for roughly five percent of all small businesses in our state and play a critical role in our economy. I will continue to https://t.co/G1YXMCYsiM

On Veterans Day, our nation pauses to honor every brave man and woman who has worn the uniform of the United States Armed Forces. We owe an eternal debt of gratitude to our veterans and their families for the immense sacrifices made in defense of our freedom and Constitution. https://t.co/PxcwHnt4vz

Today, we celebrate the 251st birthday of the United States Marine Corps and honor the legacy that began at Tun Tavern in 1775. From the halls of Montezuma to the shores of Tripoli, generations of Marines have answered the call to protect our freedom with courage and unyielding resolve. Happy Birthday to all United States Marines in Idaho and across the globe—Semper Fidelis.

From the shores of Lake Coeur d'Alene to the rolling hills of north Idaho, the Coeur d'Alene Tribe has a proud legacy of leadership and community care.  I am grateful for our continued collaboration to expand health and wellness resources in Plummer and combat domestic violence in local communities.

Idaho voters have spoken: the legendary Winchester Model 1873 is our official state gun.  This iconic firearm is a fitting symbol of Idaho's rich heritage and our steadfast commitment to defending Second Amendment freedoms.  I will always stand up for law-abiding citizens and protect the constitutional rights that make the Gem State strong.

When crisis strikes, law enforcement officers, firefighters, EMTs and dispatchers face danger to save lives. These selfless everyday heroes across Idaho risk their own safety to keep our families and neighborhoods secure. Thank you to all first responders for your unwavering bravery and dedication to public safety.

Historic drought and extreme conditions continue to exacerbate wildfires across Idaho, making the work of our courageous wildland firefighters more critical than ever.  To ensure these brave men and women have the resources they need, I am actively working with bipartisan https://t.co/3pO9mJsX96

posts.text: The @USOCC’s report provides clear evidence of political debanking and underscores the need for access to financial services to be based on objective creditworthiness rather than ideology or political preferences. I fully support @POTUS,  @USComptroller and @SecScottBessent's actions to end these discriminatory practices.

Idaho’s sugar beet growers play a vital role in powering our agriculture sector and delivering natural, high-quality sugar to American kitchens nationwide. On National Real Sugar Day, I celebrate local farm families and processors who work hard to cultivate this essential commodity.

In Idaho, 34 of our 44 counties rely on the Secure Rural Schools program to maintain local roads, support emergency services and fund public education. My bipartisan bill extends SRS for three years to ensure these communities receive the reliable federal support they are owed. I will keep fighting to provide lasting certainty for Idaho’s rural counties.

Since coming to Capitol Hill, I have made combating cancer a top legislative priority. The MCED Screening Coverage Act is a game changer that will help detect cancer when it is most treatable, improving survival rates and lowering costs for patients and providers. https://t.co/ahelxdPsLT
https://t.co/VkXkF9tUXP

Idahoans value our public lands and the incredible outdoor recreation opportunities they provide every day. That is why I support the America the Beautiful Act, to address deferred maintenance backlogs and ensure proper stewardship of our national treasures. I continue to advocate for sound, fiscally responsible policies that preserve reasonable public access to our natural resources for generations to come.

Idaho’s farmers work long hours through every season to feed, clothe and fuel our nation and world.  From potatoes and barley to dairy and cattle, Idaho farmers proudly produce the diverse agricultural products our for which our state is known.  On National Farmer’s Day, I express my profound gratitude to the hardworking families who form our state's agricultural economy and heritage.

Mental health is an essential part of overall well-being, yet too many individuals and families face challenges in silence. On World Mental Health Day, we recommit to expanding access to care, reducing stigma and supporting those in need. If you or a loved one are struggling, know that support is available—reach out, check on your neighbors and remember that help is always within reach. https://t.co/u5VaSPRs5N

Participation in sports equips young women with invaluable life lessons in discipline, teamwork, leadership and confidence. I co-sponsored the resolution designating American Girls in Sports Day to honor our female athletes and ensure Title IX protections remain intact, so biological women and girls compete on a fair, safe and level playing field. I will continue standing up for female athletes across Idaho and our nation as they strive for excellence on and off the field. https://t.co/y9KB6mvTU4

Honored to be named to @NSSF’s 2026 Dean’s List for achieving a 100-percent voting and co-sponsorship record in defense of our Second Amendment rights! Safeguarding the constitutional freedoms of law-abiding Idahoans, supporting our firearm industry and protecting America's heritage of hunting and recreational shooting will always remain a top priority of mine. Idahoans can count on me to continue fighting for our outdoor traditions and constitutional liberties in the 119th Congress.

Idaho’s 4-H programs empower young people across our state with essential skills in agriculture, leadership, STEM and civic responsibility. I am proud to co-sponsor the resolution designating National 4-H Week to celebrate the incredible mentors, parents and youth who embody the motto of making the best better. Investing in our 4-H leaders today ensures a bright and prosperous future for Idaho’s agricultural heritage.

President Trump’s Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards reset is a major affordability win that stops federal overreach and is projected to lower the cost of a new vehicle by $1,300 for American families.  By eliminating punitive Biden-era mandates and advancing my Restoring Affordability in Automobile Manufacturing Act, we can protect consumer choice and put hardworking taxpayers back in the driver's seat.

I agree with the @dcexaminer’s recent editorial highlighting how the Trump Administration’s CAFE standards reset will make cars more affordable for working families. By restoring market-driven choices and curbing bureaucratic overreach, this move—alongside my RAAM Act—trusts consumers, rather than federal bureaucrats, to choose the vehicles that best fit their lives and budgets.

Our law enforcement officers work tirelessly to keep our neighborhoods safe. Building strong, trusting relationships with the communities they serve is key to public safety. I am proud to co-lead the Senate Resolution recognizing National Community Policing Week and honoring the officers and neighborhood leaders working together across Idaho to protect our families. Thank you to all law enforcement who serve and foster connection in our communities.

I joined a bipartisan coalition of colleagues to introduce legislation reauthorizing the Secure Rural Schools program for three years.  Counties home to non-taxable federal lands deserve financial stability to support critical community needs.  This three-year extension provides rural Idaho with a predictable foundation for budget planning as we work toward a permanent funding solution.

Without clear rules of the road, college sports risk being dominated by only a handful of the wealthiest programs—endangering small and mid-sized athletic departments, Olympic sports and women's programs. Every major university in Idaho supports the Protect College Sports Act of 2026 to establish uniform national standards for Name, Image and Likeness compensation and bring stability to college athletics. I am hopeful that the House will join us in passing this critical, bipartisan legislation to ensure a fair playing field for student-athletes and schools across the country.

What an incredible finish in Moscow! @Idaho_Vandals showed true grit with a late touchdown and two-point conversion to end Montana State’s 19-game win streak. Proud of our Vandal football team for leaving it all on the field! https://t.co/d0SedWeESg

During Religious Education Week, we celebrate the faith leaders, educators and families who instill moral values, wisdom and faith in our youth. Religious education plays a vital role in shaping strong character, fostering community and preserving our nation's foundational principles of religious freedom. Thank you to all who dedicate themselves to guiding and inspiring the next generation.

America must lead the world in artificial intelligence, but everyday families should not have to pay for the massive power grids and infrastructure required by big tech data centers.  I voted to advance the Ratepayer Protection Act to ensure large-load customers pay their fair share for energy upgrades, keeping electricity bills affordable for Idaho families and local businesses.  We can power American innovation while still protecting working families from bearing the cost.  It’s unfortunate Senate Democrats failed to join us in advancing this important bill the House had already passed 417-3. https://t.co/KgD6ORdGKX

The Senate unanimously passed a resolution officially recognizing National Forensic Science Week, celebrating the dedicated professionals who work tirelessly behind the scenes to seek truth and deliver justice. From processing evidence to deploying advanced technologies, forensic experts across Idaho and our nation provide the critical analysis needed to solve complex cases and protect our communities. I am proud to join my colleagues in honoring their extraordinary service and commitment to public safety.
https://t.co/ano3TRPZsL

I joined Senators @RonWyden, @SenatorRisch and @SenJeffMerkley to introduce legislation that would reauthorize the Secure Rural Schools program through a three-year extension.  This critical program helps fulfill the federal government’s obligation to forested counties by funding schools, roads and emergency response projects.  We remain committed to delivering stability for rural families across Idaho and the West.

roll_calls.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Motion to Proceed to S. 4668
roll_calls.result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Agreed to (74-24, 3/5 majority required)
roll_calls.plain_language: This was a vote to end debate on taking up a college-sports bill on athletes' name, image, and likeness rights, agents, transfers, and a limited antitrust exemption for selling some media rights. A Yea moves the Senate toward taking up the bill. A Nay would have blocked ending debate.

roll_calls.question: Motion to Proceed to S. 4668
roll_calls.plain_language: This vote starts formal consideration of the college-sports bill on athletes' name, image, and likeness rights, agents, and transfers. A Yea takes up the bill. A Nay refuses to take it up.

roll_calls.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Cruz Amdt. No. 6776
roll_calls.result: Cloture Motion Agreed to (70-21, 3/5 majority required)
roll_calls.plain_language: This vote would end debate on a substitute that rewrites the college-sports bill as the Protect College Sports Act, covering athlete publicity rights, agents, medical coverage, transfers, and college-sports broadcasts. A Yea limits debate on that rewrite. A Nay keeps debate open.

roll_calls.question: Amdt. No. 6776
roll_calls.plain_language: This substitute rewrites the college-sports bill as the Protect College Sports Act, covering athlete publicity rights, agents, medical coverage, transfers, and college-sports broadcasts. A Yea adopts that rewrite. A Nay would have left the earlier text.

roll_calls.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: S. 4668, as Amended
roll_calls.result: Cloture Motion Agreed to (74-25, 3/5 majority required)
roll_calls.plain_language: This vote would end debate on the college-sports bill after it was rewritten as the Protect College Sports Act. A Yea limits debate so the Senate can move to a final passage vote. A Nay keeps debate open.

roll_calls.question: Baldwin Amdt. No. 6828
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment rewrites the college-sports bill's preemption section so states generally cannot set conflicting rules on athlete publicity pay, transfers, or certain eligibility, while keeping state civil-rights, contract, privacy, and similar laws unless they conflict. A Yea adopts that text. A Nay rejects it.

roll_calls.question: Paul Amdt. No. 6758
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment would have replaced the college-sports bill with the Collegiate Sports Integrity Act, which centers on an antitrust exemption for athletic conferences and associations. A Yea would have made that swap. A Nay rejected it.

roll_calls.question: Kennedy Amdt. No. 6760
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment would have barred colleges, conferences, and athletic associations from raising ticket prices for a sport by more than 4 percent from the prior academic year. A Yea would have added that cap. A Nay rejected it.

roll_calls.question: Booker Amdt. No. 6805
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment would have capped a student-athlete insurance and catastrophic-injury fund at $200 million and required major conferences and an athletic association to cover any amount above $100 million. A Yea would have set that cap. A Nay rejected it.

roll_calls.question: Booker Amdt. No. 6835
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment would have let coaches move between four-year colleges under transfer rules like those for athletes, and it would have voided a coach's endorsement deal unless the pay matched similar non-coaches and had a real business purpose. A Yea would have added those rules. A Nay rejected them.

roll_calls.question: S. 4668, as amended
roll_calls.plain_language: The Senate passed the college-sports bill as rewritten into the Protect College Sports Act, covering athlete publicity rights, agents, medical coverage, transfers, and college-sports broadcasts. A Yea passes that bill. A Nay votes no.
